subject.title: security(audit): warn on plugin load paths and SecretRef env fallback

question: Should an active, intentionally supported SecretRef environment fallback make the default Doctor gateway-auth contribution unhealthy, or should that warning remain limited to security audit and explicit lint selection?
rationale: The code can detect the state reliably, but only maintainers can define whether supported environment fallback is an ordinary compatibility path or a security posture problem that default Doctor should continually flag.

options.title: Audit plus opt-in Doctor
options.body: Keep the security-audit warning and register the Doctor check for explicit or --all lint selection without changing routine Doctor health.

options.title: Warn in default Doctor
options.body: Adopt environment fallback as a default warning-level health problem and document that intentional users should expect the warning until they remove the fallback.

options.title: Audit only
options.body: Remove the Doctor check and keep the posture signal solely in openclaw security audit.

recommendation.title: Audit plus opt-in Doctor
recommendation.body: Keep the security-audit warning and register the Doctor check for explicit or --all lint selection without changing routine Doctor health.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses Gateway auth, SecretRef policy, Doctor semantics, and security-audit posture, matching this person's recent cross-boundary history.
